title: Migrate Gemini Workflows with Evidence
summary: Inventory dependencies, separate portable contracts from Gemini-specific behavior, compare SDKs, models or providers, canary safely, and preserve rollback through lifecycle changes.
objectives: Inventory Gemini API, SDK, model, prompt, content, tool, state, safety, data, and operational dependencies.
Separate portable application contracts from Gemini-specific capabilities.
Use current model, SDK, and deprecation evidence plus controlled evaluation.
Migrate with coexistence, canary gates, reconciliation, rollback, and accountable closeout.

sections.title: Inventory before changing
paragraphs: Find each SDK and version, credential path, model reference, API version, system instruction, content and part parser, chat state, function schema and response, safety setting, modality, file, data control, evaluation, dashboard, alert, cost assumption, and runbook.

Include AI Studio prototypes, legacy libraries, Gemini API and Google Cloud variants, ADK agents, hosted tools, caches, batches, and shadow clients. Give each dependency an owner, source, risk, and verification method.

sections.title: Separate portable and Gemini-specific contracts
paragraphs: User outcomes, application schemas, authorization policy, evaluation rubrics, telemetry fields, postconditions, and incident rules can remain portable. Candidate parts, finish reasons, safety settings, function-response protocol, model controls, hosted tools, and ADK behavior may be Gemini-specific.

Create explicit adapters without pretending models, APIs, or providers are identical. Preserve native capability where it matters and expose unsupported behavior rather than silently weakening safety, quality, accessibility, or evidence.

code.label: Portable contract with a Gemini adapter

sections.title: Use current lifecycle evidence
paragraphs: For SDK migration, compare package, client construction, request and response types, async and streaming behavior, errors, retries, credentials, and feature support. For model changes, compare modalities, tools, limits, settings, safety, latency, usage, and quality.

Verify model status and announced earliest shutdown dates from current official model and deprecation pages. Track previews and legacy libraries proactively with owners; do not copy today's model names into durable architecture.
sections.callout: A compiling SDK or model substitution can still regress state, safety, tools, output, latency, cost, or data handling.

sections.title: Evaluate, shadow, and canary
paragraphs: Run baseline and candidate against identical representative, multimodal, edge, adversarial, incident, and holdout cases. Compare output, factuality, safety blocks, structured data, state, tool trajectories, latency, usage, and cost by critical slice.

Use offline replay, shadow traffic, or a small canary only where policy permits. Define promotion, hold, and rollback thresholds first; isolate telemetry by version and reconcile possible side effects before shifting traffic.

code.label: Normalize outcomes across APIs before a canary gate

sections.title: Migrate reversibly and close deliberately
paragraphs: Use configurable routing, versioned prompts and adapters, compatible record changes, dual-read or dual-run patterns when justified, and rehearsed rollback. Keep old and new state and safety mappings explicit until observation passes.

Close after production gates pass, rollback and reconciliation are proven, privacy and security review is complete, documentation is current, deprecated use is resolved or accepted with an owner, and residual risk is acknowledged. Migration away from Gemini follows the same evidence discipline.

activity.title: Plan and rehearse a Gemini migration
instructions: Inventory one workflow across SDK, API, model, credentials, prompts, parts, state, tools, safety, modalities, data, evaluation, telemetry, and operations.
Build a portable-versus-Gemini-specific matrix and map each incompatibility to an adapter, redesign, explicit non-support, data migration, or operational change.
Use synthetic no-paid-call fixtures for a baseline/candidate evaluation and define offline, shadow or canary promotion, hold, rollback, reconciliation, and deprecation-exit criteria.
Rehearse a failed canary and record detection, decision, rollback time, state and side-effect reconciliation, communication, owners, and closeout evidence.
evidence: A dependency inventory and compatibility matrix linked to current SDK, model, lifecycle, and troubleshooting sources.
A comparison report, rollout plan, successful rollback and reconciliation rehearsal, and signed closeout checklist.

cues.text: Ask learners to classify one part, safety, or tool behavior as portable, adapter concern, or provider-specific.
Allow three minutes to write a rollback trigger and state-reconciliation check before viewing candidate results.
Check that rollback was rehearsed and no lifecycle dependency, state mapping, or risk lacks an owner.
Guide inventory, compatibility, evaluation, rollout gates, rollback rehearsal, reconciliation, and closeout.
Begin the check after the learner can migrate without assuming equivalence or sacrificing safety, data, evidence, or rollback.

questions.prompt: What happens before changing an SDK or model?
choices: Inventory dependencies and current official evidence
questions.explanation: References participate in broader behavioral, state, data, and operational contracts.

questions.prompt: Which contract is usually most portable?
choices: A user outcome and application validation schema
questions.explanation: Application-owned outcomes can remain stable behind adapters.

questions.prompt: What should an SDK migration compare?
choices: Client, requests, responses, streaming, errors, retries, credentials, and feature behavior
questions.explanation: SDK migration changes multiple application contracts.

questions.prompt: When are canary rollback thresholds defined?

choices: Production gates, proven rollback and reconciliation, current docs, resolved lifecycle use, and owned risk
questions.explanation: Closeout requires production and operational evidence.
